errors.claim: Consultative styles such as "we'll bring it to them for buy-in" are symptoms of insufficient up-front involvement, and this framing runs through every subsequent interaction design.
errors.searches: "we'll bring it to them for buy-in"; "consultative"; "buy-in"; "all about creating ownership"
errors.source_check: The source contrasts ownership with buy-in and says Liberating Structures are about ownership, but it contains neither the quoted consultative formulation nor an explicit claim about every subsequent design.

errors.claim: Small tables are generally much better than big tables because large conference tables inhibit conversation.
errors.source_check: The source qualifies "SMALL tables are much better than big tables" with "if you plan to have participants do some work that requires writing or drawing." The reference omits that condition and broadens the claim.

errors.claim: The worked complaints are "supplies never brings enough gloves" and "doctors need to round on MRSA-positive patients last."
errors.searches: "supplies never"; "wear gloves"; "MRSA-positive"; "change their behavior by rounding"
errors.source_check: The source says, "Well, we would wear gloves if we had the supplies, but they never bring enough" and "The doctors need to change their behavior by rounding on MRSA positive patients last." Both reference quotations are compressed paraphrases, not essentially verbatim.

errors.claim: The handbook calls "Who's not here that could contribute to our conversation?" "one of the most important questions you can ask."
errors.searches: "one of the most important"; "may be one"; "Who's not here"
errors.source_check: The source says, "This may be one of the most important questions you can ask." The reference removes the modal "may be" and strengthens the claim.

errors.claim: Each Take a Panel sheet must "stand alone — that can be understood without explanation by someone who comes by."
errors.source_check: The source says, "Make sure the result is a 'stand alone' that can be understood without explanation by someone who comes by." The reference inserts an em dash into the quotation and recasts the source wording.

errors.claim: Report-outs typically "drain the life out of whatever conversation that took place in the small group."
errors.source_check: The source reads, "it typically drains the life out of whatever conversation that took place in the small group." The quoted verb was changed from "drains" to "drain."

errors.claim: In Wise Crowds phase three, the client rejoins for approximately 15 minutes.
errors.searches: "Here's what I heard"; "for example, 15 minutes"; "amount of time set"; "at least 15 minutes"
errors.source_check: The source says the conversation continues "for the amount of time set, for example, 15 minutes." Fifteen minutes is an example, not the stated general duration.

errors.claim: The Wise Crowds timing prescription is: client describes for about 10 minutes, team discusses for at least 15 minutes, and client rejoins for about 15 minutes.
errors.searches: "about 10 minutes"; "at least 15 minutes"; "for example, 15 minutes"; "amount of time set"
errors.source_check: The first two timings are prescriptions, but the third is only an example of a facilitator-set duration. The statistics row hardens it into a general timing prescription.

errors.claim: The handbook attributes the What–So What–Now What question structure to the Center for Creative Leadership.
errors.searches: "Center for Creative Leadership"; "included many"; "developed by"; "following questions in the following order"
errors.source_check: The source says the exercise is included in many Center for Creative Leadership programmes and links to CCL. It does not say CCL originated or supplied the question structure.

errors.claim: Conversation Café has three rounds plus a final round.
errors.source_check: The source labels four stages as Round 1, Round 2, Dialogue, and Final Round. It does not identify Dialogue as a third round.

errors.claim: On the Levels of Accountability page, "Learn & Grow" and "Empowered" form a top band while "Protect & Defend" and "Disempowered" form a bottom band.
errors.source_check: All four labels occur in the converted source, but the text does not state their top/bottom placement or call them bands. That spatial relationship cannot be verified from the supplied source text.

errors.claim: Diana Whitney is also implicitly connected to Appreciative Interviews through that section's Appreciative Inquiry pointer.
errors.source_check: The source names Whitney in Q Storming and separately says Appreciative Interviews belong to Appreciative Inquiry. The Appreciative Interviews section does not name or explicitly connect Whitney.

errors.claim: The Center for Creative Leadership is the source for the What–So What–Now What framing.
errors.source_check: The source establishes that CCL uses the exercise in many programmes, not that CCL originated or is the source of the framing.
